2:
### Cardinalities, slots and explicit relationship changes

Recommended initial rule: each draft has one owning project or explicit Unassigned and at most one native campaign, consistent with the current campaign_id contract. Its private working title belongs to the draft. It can appear in multiple saved collections, which are projections and consume no slots; it has at most one primary content-family membership in that same project. A family does not own campaign membership or grant source access. Multiple causal source/derivation references are allowed with exact pins and permitted access, including an authorized cross-project reference, but never automatic membership or copying. The campaign slot is charged once to its actual admitted draft/channel/format under native rules; a second collection or source link does not consume another slot.

A family is an optional Content Desk grouping with a stable identity and same-project membership. Detaching a draft removes that membership without deleting its source, siblings, history or receipts. Archiving a family hides the grouping, not every member. Moving a draft previews project, family, campaign and restricted references separately; a family in project A cannot remain the primary family of a draft moved to B. Cross-project citations may remain only where both permissions and method allow them. An active release remains bound to its historical package/scope; the move is blocked or explicitly deferred until that constraint can be safely resolved. No hidden cascade reschedules siblings. Supporting the same artifact in two campaigns is a later explicit native cardinality change, not achieved by duplicating its ID or charging it twice.

Concrete trace: source S1 in Founder writing supports family F1 with drafts D1 and D2; a permitted pinned reference from app campaign C2 supports independent draft D3 in project Aster. D1 and D2 may each belong to one campaign or none. A collection called Launch examples can display all three without owning them. Moving D2 to Aster preserves D2/revisions, requires explicit F1 detach and campaign remap, verifies S1 access and leaves D1's active release unchanged. If D2 itself has an admitted release that cannot tolerate the move, the preview refuses it until resolved. These are proposed relationship rules to reconcile in source application.

### An operation key binds one exact intended effect

Every mutating owner command stores a canonical request fingerprint with its operation key: actor/owning scope, action, native target and expected base revision, exact package, destination and timing when applicable. Same key with the same fingerprint returns the prior admitted result. Same key with a changed fingerprint returns Operation conflict and exposes the original permitted result; it cannot report success for the new request. Lookup is authorization-checked and retained at least through the operation/recovery lifetime defined by the native owner; eviction must not silently make an uncertain request safe to repeat.

A parent plan operation groups stable child command keys and individual receipts, not one reusable key for every mutation. An intentional second import/copy carries a new explicit import-intent identity or nonce chosen as Create separate copy in the preview. A retry reuses the prior identity. Changing r2 to r3 or account A to B after a lost response requires reconciliation of the old action first, then a separate authorized intent if still wanted. The captured ReleaseWithOptions returns a prior key result without comparing the changed payload, while Enqueue does not itself establish deduplication; both need compatible owner changes. Existing body/update/approval/suggestion DTOs also lack the proposed revision guards. The UI must not imply that adding a correlation field alone solves these contracts.
4:
### A concrete immutable package basis

Synthetic package P2 for D1/r2 contains the exact structured text representation and body digest, format text-only, ordered empty media list, link set, author-expression identity Owner, revision producer external assistant plus owner edits, method pin M0.6 with adapter pin A0.1, and claim C1 anchored to the exact structural sentence at body r2. Source S1/r3 supports the structural statement; no timing claim is qualified. Its editorial decision scope is wording only and destination is unbound. Its digest covers a canonical manifest whose field normalization is defined by the native owner. Example labels P2/S1 are synthetic record names, not fabricated cryptographic digests or existing production IDs.

For an illustrated variant, each media entry must name the immutable asset version and actual byte digest, placement/order, aspect/crop coordinates, caption and alt text. Unknown or unavailable original bytes remain unresolved; no digest is inferred from a filename. Completing a pending-media slot produces P3 even when body r2 is unchanged. The earlier wording-only decision can remain applicable if no wording changed, while the new media/full-package decision is pending. Cropping, links, attribution, method basis and accessibility text are versioned package inputs rather than mutable decoration.

Use UTF-16 code-unit offsets only after the Content Desk owner adopts and verifies that explicit convention, paired with body revision, quoted-span digest and context anchor. Current citation DTOs expose integer spans without a declared unit/revision. Any offset mismatch, ambiguous moved text or changed quoted span makes the anchor stale and unverified; never leave a green underline on unrelated text after an emoji insertion. Structured thread items anchor to item identity plus the same revision-bound convention. Current permissions, asset release, source freshness, consent, account eligibility and time authority are revalidated at action time; their latest status is not frozen as perpetual permission inside the digest.
5:
### The job and accounting contract must match the selected route

The current CommissionAgentWork request exposes draft ID/action and result status/body; it does not establish selected-span binding, context/method pins, per-request budget, cancellation or usage. The richer help sheet therefore requires a route capability record before its controls are enabled. A job manifest pins draft/base/span, allowed context and recipient/provider, adopted method/adapter, requested output, runner/profile and budget scope. Each attempt has a stable job/attempt identity and observed usage basis; all candidates, failed attempts and partial outputs belong in the accounting view, not just the adopted candidate.

The selected native runner/provider's budget owner must reserve or otherwise enforce the authorized maximum across concurrent jobs. Prose's session budget/candidate accounting can be reused within its actual route, but is not proof of enforcement for an Agent Manager request. If reliable enforcement is unavailable, do not offer a promised hard ceiling; choose a bounded supported route or keep manual/external authoring. Unknown charges reserve an unresolved amount and stop new spending that could exceed the approved scope until reconciled. Idempotent result lookup is not a new billable attempt.

Cancel is offered only when the route supports it, and its label explains whether it stops new work or can abort already accepted provider work. Cancel requested does not erase incurred costs. Two jobs against the same paragraph retain their separate bases; only a selected candidate may be adopted after comparison with current text/method. A method change while generation runs does not rewrite the job's original pin. A stale result remains recoverable as a candidate, never silently current.
6:
### Stable preparation identity precedes Planner projection

Content Desk should own a proposed MarketingWorkItem with stable ID, project, occurrence when recurring, linked draft/family dependencies, task meaning, remaining-effort estimate and source revision. Its canonical source key is owner Content Desk + work ID + occurrence, not a displayed label or list position. A proof check shared by D1/D2/D3 is one work object whose dependent set has three members. Source projection admission maps that key to one Planner work projection; accepted allocations reference that projection and keep native Planner IDs.

Updating remaining effort or a deadline increments the source constraint revision and invalidates unaccepted allocation proposals. It does not silently move an accepted reservation; the user sees a conflict/change proposal. Removing two dependent variants leaves the shared work when still needed by the third. Removing the final dependency marks it no longer required and proposes a permitted cancellation, retaining prior allocations/history. Source archive/deletion emits a tombstone under the adapter contract. A completed Planner focus session records time spent; Content Desk owns whether the proof check actually succeeded. If the source is unavailable, completion remains pending rather than guessed.

The captured Planner work DTO has source_label but no source-object key. The source-adapter design is still planned. A compatible registration, identity mapping, deduplication, source revision and tombstone contract is required before the UI promises shared-work reservations. Native allocation Preview/Apply remains a second admission with its own proposal ID/revision/receipt. Replaying a projection is not replaying an allocation, and neither creates a publication schedule.
8:
### Command, actor and authority mapping

Adopt edit is an author operation: guard the exact saved/local base, create a new native body revision and preserve producer provenance. Record craft verdict is a reviewer assessment through the compatible native review route; it may be performed by an authorized agent or human, and does not own claim truth. Accept wording is a proposed scoped human editorial-decision record for an immutable package, available only after that narrower contract exists. It is not a renamed ApproveDraft call and never satisfies the existing human operator release-readiness gate by implication.

Approve native draft remains the human-operator-only native action under verified-claim, active-type, identity and lane conditions. The captured request takes draft ID, identity_id and lane; an account-free wording decision cannot truthfully fill it. Authorize release is the separately bounded human permission for the exact destination/action/window, followed by Channel Manager admission under its supported command. A human who holds all roles may see a concise combined review with every scope explicitly stated and separate receipts, avoiding redundant ritual; the system must still record and validate each native obligation. An agent's positive review plus supported-but-unverified evidence cannot pass the human operator or claim-verification gate.

This mapping supersedes any earlier interpretation that the all-fields package is required merely to assess wording, or that wording acceptance alone approves a native draft for publication. The final release package still includes all consequential fields. Until scoped editorial acceptance exists, the product may record a clearly labeled assessment and preserve the draft; it must not render an enabled control whose effect claims unsupported approval. Source application must resolve the exact enum/event names without weakening these meanings.

### Ordered external items and the meaning of partial

The inspected native partial result describes a published root post with failed first comment; its single post ID/URL and completion callback do not model a general thread. A multi-item/thread route requires an explicit extension: stable item IDs, order/dependency edges, immutable per-item content/media, per-item attempt IDs and an append-oriented receipt history. Aggregate Pending, Dispatching, Partial, Unknown, Complete or Cancelled is derived from that history and never substitutes for it. Native first-comment partial maps to root complete plus first-comment failure under its own item role.

Every external item must begin under still-valid time/consent/eligibility authority. Reaching the latest allowed instant stops new suffix dispatch; it does not retract a completed prefix. An item already in flight can return a late receipt after expiry. Reconciliation appends that fact to the original attempt and prevents a duplicate repair, regardless of receipt arrival order. A continuation references only unresolved original item identities and needs fresh authority where scope expired. A correction links its new items to the old ones rather than replacing history.

Concrete failure trace: thread items T1 and T2 have receipts, T3's request timed out, then the window expires. State is Partial with T3 outcome unknown; no new suffix or full-thread retry is allowed. A late T3 receipt makes the actual thread complete at its real observed times while preserving the earlier uncertainty. If T3 is proven not admitted, a separately authorized continuation may submit it once. Existing CompleteRelease's treatment of partial as terminal must be reconciled rather than assumed to permit this expanded repair.

### Concurrent asset use honors the same policy

Retain the current prohibition on cross-identity reuse of a published asset. To make it safe for concurrent queues, recommend Channel Manager-owned atomic asset-use reservations at release admission, keyed by the actual asset identity/version and applicable policy scope. Competing identities cannot both dispatch while an earlier reservation is admitted, in flight or unknown. The winner returns a reservation receipt; the loser returns a conflict with only the permitted identity/action detail. A missing completion response retains the reservation until reconciliation. Definite cancellation before any external effect may release it; confirmed publication retains the policy association.

The inspected code checks AssetPublications before release but records the association after completion; no runtime race was reproduced, and dispatch-time reservation semantics are not established. The proposed reservation closes that observed source gap. It is not a new public reuse permission, and reimporting identical bytes remains an invalid workaround. Legitimate cross-identity reuse still requires a separate policy decision with rights, transparency and platform evidence.
9:
### Observation identity survives correction and reconciliation

An immutable observation identifies native release/item and exact package, metric definition/version or qualitative question, collection route, observation time, covered interval, unit/denominator when meaningful and evidence basis. Provider observations retain provider event/sample identity. A correction is a new observation with corrects/supersedes relation, not an overwritten value. Repeating the identical imported event returns its prior result; a conflicting same-ID payload is held for reconciliation. A seven-day click count cannot replace a lifetime count merely because both are called clicks.

Owner-reported and provider-verified observations can be linked as corroborating or conflicting, while both original bases remain available. The selected current projection explains its inclusion and comparison rules. Missing denominator/window prevents the affected comparison; it need not prevent saving the honest incomplete observation. Qualitative evidence has a permitted attribution scope that can differ from the person's public identity. An accepted learning conclusion references the exact observations it used and becomes Needs recheck when one is corrected.

The captured native metric/publish read models are draft-focused and do not expose this full window, denominator, package or correction lineage. Extend the rightful Channel Manager/Content Desk owner records or their versioned related records before promising it. Learn is the view, not a second metrics database. Two accounts using one variant keep separate release/item identities and are not added into one success total without an explicit comparable aggregation rule.
